A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same fractional-order spiking-network research, renamed from fspikeDE to f-SNN. Their main text, appendices, equations, figures, and tables are readable and support a reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original image classification, graph node classification, link prediction, robustness, and resource-use results in Section 4 and Appendix S4.

after.justification: v2 reports original vision and graph experiments, including retained link-prediction results, new benchmark evaluations, ablations, robustness tests, and energy analyses in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: v1 specifies augmented fractional-adjoint training and a loss on the terminal accumulated-spike state in Section 3.3 and Appendix S3.2. v2 describes surrogate-gradient backpropagation through fractional updates; Appendix E replaces adjoint integrators with odeint/fdeint and illustrates a time-averaged prediction loss. These revise the documented training and readout procedure, while retaining the underlying fractional dynamics and ABM predictor.

E1.justification: v2 adds event-based N-MNIST, DVS-Lip and HarDVS, plus CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet evaluations, while removing static MNIST and Fashion-MNIST experiments. CS/Physics node classification disappears, but link prediction on those datasets remains. Temporal jitter, truncation and frame-loss tests also broaden the evaluated input conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds snnTorch implementations to graph and vision comparisons and removes the separate I-fspikeDE rows from the main comparisons. An alpha=1 control remains in the new ablation table. MSG is removed from node classification but retained against SpikingJelly for link prediction. New vision neuron comparisons also evaluate conventional IF against fractional IF.

E3.justification: The retained SGCN/DRSGNN split, batch size and timestep settings remain unchanged. New evaluations introduce Transformer training specified as 500 epochs in Appendix D.1.2, four-timestep static-image experiments, and 160×160 ImageNet inputs. v2 also introduces a normalized corruption score and changes energy accounting to include neuron-intrinsic costs, which v1's synaptic-operation calculation omitted.

E4.justification: v2 adds fixed-versus-learnable fractional-order, network-width, neuron-type and memory-window studies, plus temporal-corruption tests and occluded feature-map visualizations. Graph feature masking moves from Photo/Computers to Cora/Citeseer, while edge dropping changes in the opposite direction. v1's separate spike-noise injection analysis is removed. These substantially change the questions tested beyond ordinary benchmark accuracy.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 independent graph runs and report means with standard deviations, including link prediction. Vision results remain point estimates. v2 introduces no new seed-reporting practice, confidence intervals or significance tests; additional comparator rows follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive benchmark, ablation, robustness and energy results and removes older static-vision, MSG node-classification and training-memory comparison entries. The CNN DVS128Gesture result changes from 95.87% to 94.80% under the revised training description, so it is not a controlled same-setting performance comparison. N-Caltech101's 70.26%, retained SGCN/DRSGNN accuracies and MSG link-prediction results are unchanged. New SpikFormer totals are 2.933723 mJ for LIF and 2.911792 mJ for fractional LIF.

T1.justification: v1's Mittag-Leffler relaxation lemma and proof are retained as Proposition 1 with an explicit subthreshold assumption. v2 adds perturbation and spike-timing derivations, finite-LIF-ensemble irreducibility using Grünwald-Letnikov dynamics, and a spike-train irreducibility corollary with proofs in Appendix C. The adjoint derivation and backward-memory analysis are removed. The new corollary's proof contains an inconsistent threshold inequality in Equation 51.

C1.justification: The adjoint-training algorithm and reduced-training-memory claims cease to be central contributions in v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion. v2 instead emphasizes compatibility across established architectures and new theoretical claims about finite-ensemble irreducibility and robustness. The broad claims concerning long-term dependencies, accuracy, noise robustness and comparable energy efficiency remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets expressivity through a continuum of timescales and explicitly qualifies theoretical robustness advantages as regime-dependent in Appendix C.2. Its energy discussion now explains how lower synaptic activity offsets additional fractional-neuron costs. It also discusses memory-window tradeoffs and adds practical limitations concerning distributed training and missing CuPy-style acceleration.

D1.justification: v2 discloses selected graph fractional orders in Table 4, identifies additional backbone and training configurations, and substantially expands custom-neuron and SNNWrapper usage examples. It replaces v1's per-dataset CNN architecture/firing-rate tables with detailed SpikFormer accounting. Code-access guidance changes from v1's repository hyperlink to supplementary code and a zip archive referenced by the new reproducibility statement.

R1.justification: v2 removes the dedicated adjoint/neural-ODE training positioning and substantially expands distinctions from fractional biological models, shallow fractional networks, fractional PINNs and fractional-gradient optimizers. New discussions include Rombouts and Bohte, Zhang et al. and modern ALIF/GLIF/CLIF/PSN families. It also explicitly claims the first generalizable framework for end-to-end fractional SNN training.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, introduction, related-work narrative and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Neuromorphic experiments precede graph experiments, static-image evaluations move to the appendix, and theory gains a central section. References move before the appendices, which are reorganized, and reproducibility and ethics statements are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds biological/circuit illustrations, redesigned dynamics and memory diagrams, a robustness radar chart, occluded feature maps and numerous ablation displays. Accuracy tables are restructured, robustness plots redrawn, and CNN resource tables replaced by detailed layerwise energy tables. The existing Mittag-Leffler plot moves from v1's appendix Figure 5 to v2's main-text Figure 3.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through broader benchmarks, fractional-order and memory ablations, and accounting for neuron costs omitted in v1. However, its new central spike-train proof sets theta=5h_T/4 tending to zero while Equation 51 requires 1<theta. Table 11's noise score of 95.96 also conflicts with approximately 97.58 obtained from its entries and stated formula. These reliability problems in new theoretical and robustness evidence prevent a confident net quality judgment despite the substantial empirical gains.
